newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - SEPT 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - SEPT 3.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
U.S. LAUNCHES MISSILE RAIDS ON BAGHDAD
US President Bill Clinton ordered a cruise missile attack on Iraq this morning in response to Saddam Hussein's invasion of the Kurdish safe haven.
WATCHDOGS TO POUNCE ON HK FUND MANAGERS

Investment Management Regulation Organisation (IMRO) officials will fly out to Hong Kong to take part in joint inspections of British fund managers with the colony's Securities and Futures Commission. This follows the harshest disciplinary action ever taken by the colony's watchdog, against Jardine Fleming Investment Management.
The dollar, traditionally seen as a safe currency in times of international crisis, rose to 109.25 yen from 109.165 yesterday.
LABOUR SET TO WOO BUSINESS LEADERS
Labour's campaign to attract business leaders will culminate tomorrow with a London conference hosted by Tony Blair and his shadow cabinet and the publication of the party's Business Prospectus.
BURFORD SET FOR 100 MLN STG WAREHOUSES SPIN-OFF

Burford Holdings is in the process of appointing advisers for the spin off of specialist retail warehouses arm Grantchester, its third demerger in 18 months. Grantchester is likely to be valued at 100 million stg, and Burford will retain a 25 percent stake in Grantchester.
LUCAS CHIEF PUTS FAITH IN AEROSPACE

Sir Brian Pearse, the chairman of Lucas Industries, has said the group will be aiming for further expansion in areas like flight control equipment, once the merger with Varity is completed later this year.
